newsitem.title: GERMANY: Some BHF mark repos to stay in London.
newsitem.headline: Some BHF mark repos to stay in London.

text.p: Germany's BHF-Bank AG said on Wednesday it planned to retain a small amount of its repo business in marks in London, but the business would remain strongly focused in Frankfurt.

"We will continue to do some business in London but we have been expanding this business massively in Frankfurt in the last year and a half," a spokesman for the second-tier German bank said in response to a Reuters query.
"We want to continue with this business in the UK with an eye on further developments in economic and monetary union (EMU)," he said.
Earlier, Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG, two of Germany's three biggest banks said they planned to repatriate their securities repurchase business in marks from London.

The moves follow the Bundesbank's decision in December to remove minimum reserve requirements from certain securities repurchase transactions, partly answering banks' calls to have this alleged competitive disadvantage removed.
Under the minimum reserves system, banks are required to hold non-interest-bearing deposits at the central bank.

However the Bundesbank said at the time that it was still convinced of the usefulness of minimum reserves in general and would continue to lobby to have the system adopted by the future European Central Bank.
